We are a team of enthusiastic engineering students who are passionate about space, technology, innovation, and solving real-world problems. We are interested in exploring NASA’s data and creating practical, creative solutions using technology.
Our interests include engineering, programming, AI/ML, data analysis, astronomy, Earth observation, and problem-solving. We are beginners in some areas but are eager to learn, experiment, and work together as a team.
summary:
Project Name: ApolloX
Project Title : JUNIOR ASTRONAUT MISSION TRAINER(JAMT)
For the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, Team ApolloX developed the Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer (JAMT), an immersive web and mobile simulation platform designed to make aerospace science accessible to young learners aged 8 to 16. JAMT addresses the challenge of youth STEM engagement by translating authentic astronaut training hurdles—such as G-force physics, orbital docking vectors, and Mars communication relays—into interactive, gamified modules.
​Grounded directly in official NASA open-source datasets and APIs (including the Horizons API and Planetary Fact Sheets), JAMT bridges raw scientific telemetry with intuitive gameplay. This project is vital because it converts passive screen time into active, inquiry-based cognitive learning, empowering the next generation of explorers to visualize and pursue futures in space exploration and STEM fields.
details:
JUNIOR ASTRONAUT MISSION TRAINER(JAMT)-TEAM ApolloX

What does it do & How does it work?

The Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer (JAMT) is an interactive, web and mobile-ready simulation platform designed for young explorers aged 8 to 16. It gamifies authentic astronaut selection and flight training procedures by translating complex aerospace science into intuitive modules. Powered by official NASA open data—including the NASA Horizons API for real-time ephemeris calculations, Planetary Fact Sheets for gravity parameters, and the Exoplanet Archive for landing site topography—users guide simulations through physical balance sensors, orbital docking physics engines, and deep-space communication delay challenges.

What benefits & intended impact does it have?

JAMT converts passive screen time into active cognitive learning, bridging the gap between raw scientific data and youth education. By making aerospace science engaging and approachable, JAMT inspires children to visualize and pursue long-term futures in STEM fields.

What tools , coding languages , softwares , and hardwares did you use?

  • Fronted:React.js / Progressive Web App (PWA) framework for zero-install cross-device compatibility across school Chromebooks, tablets, and mobile devices.
  • Rendering & physics : Three.js and Canvas 2D for smooth, interactive 3D spacecraft rendering and real-time orbital calculations.
  • Backend & APIs : Node.js server infrastructure handling secure REST querying of NASA endpoints and user progress tracking.

Hardware : Standard mobile/tablet device motion sensors (accelerometers and gyroscopes) for physical conditioning and G-force simulation modules.

How is your project creative & what factors did your team consider?

JAMT stands out through its novel combination of gamified human physiology training with real-time astronomical ephemeris data. Team ApolloX carefully considered accessibility (including screen-reader support, adjustable high-contrast visual modes, and multilingual localization) to ensure that students of all abilities can experience the wonder and rigor of space exploration.
